properties.name: The design can state that two parts must agree, and check it — correspondence as a first-class rule
properties.statement:
NOT FROM reflow. Raised 2026-07-28 from the architecture-description standard ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010, after Anthony's instruction to bring judgement rather than treat reflow's workflows as canon. reflow had nothing resembling this; the gap is visible only against the standard practice reflow2 exists to serve.

42010 models an architecture description as Stakeholders holding Concerns, Viewpoints that frame those concerns, and Views governed by viewpoints — and then the piece that does the work: CORRESPONDENCES between elements of different views, governed by CORRESPONDENCE RULES that state what must hold between them, so consistency is a checkable claim rather than a hope. reflow2 has the projection half and not the correspondence half. dec:views-are-projections is right and is stronger than anything in reflow (a view is a pure projection of the graph; renderer fill-ins are defects), but a projection guarantees only that a view does not invent — it says nothing about whether two projections of the same design agree where they overlap.

WHAT reflow2 HAS TODAY IS A HANDFUL OF HARDCODED CORRESPONDENCES. cap:seam-incompatibility says when two linked designs disagree at a boundary. reconcile_artifacts, reconcile_deployment and reconcile_verification each compare the design against one facet of reality. The unvalidated_capability, status_contradiction and unprovided_interface gaps are each a fixed rule about what must agree with what. Every one is a correspondence rule expressed in Rust, invisible to the user, and unextendable: a team cannot say "in OUR design, every Component with concern=safety must have a Verification of kind=validation performed in a non-simulation Environment" and have it checked. The rules that exist are the ones the maintainer thought of.

WHY IT MATTERS HERE SPECIFICALLY. The operating context is several organisations with competing, partially-built designs that were never meant to interoperate, delivered as increments. That is the situation 42010's correspondence machinery was written for: A's view and B's view describe overlapping reality with different vocabulary and different concerns, and what makes integration tractable is being able to STATE the correspondence and then compute whether it still holds as both sides move. Hand-wiring each such rule into the tool does not scale past the maintainer's imagination.

AND IT WOULD GIVE Requirement.concern A READER. concern is the sharpest item in the 2026-07-28 sweep — an enum carrying the ILS/SME vocabulary (logistics, sustainment, safety, security…), single-valued at `core` on 67 of 67, with no writer on the MCP surface and no reader anywhere, so "which are the safety requirements?" answers `none` rather than `unknown`. It is dead because nothing consumes concerns, and nothing consumes concerns because there is no stakeholder-concern-viewpoint chain for them to feed. Building the chain is what would make that property mean something, rather than deleting it.

OPEN and not decided: whether a correspondence rule is authored as data (a small predicate over node types, properties and edges, evaluated by the detector machinery) or remains code with only the VOCABULARY made explicit; whether Stakeholder is a new node type or Actor grown up (Actor already carries actor_type including `stakeholder`, and is currently counted in report.rs and read nowhere — see req:scenarios-are-modelled); and how a user-authored rule avoids becoming a way to make the tool assert things nobody checked, which dec:report-dont-judge would forbid.
